signals.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
signals.content: Recent autonomous machine learning engineering (MLE) agents have made significant progress on public leaderboards. Often motivated by progress stagnation over long-horizon cycles and limited Large Language Model (LLM) primitives, modern MLE agents are deployed on top of increasingly elaborate machinery: multi-agent orchestrators, dedicated retrieval subagents, and more. While such harnesses expand, the use of more primitive but improved coding agents - where LLMs have direct access to the execution environment through read, write, and bash primitives - has received little attention in the field. In this paper we find that, under an equal time budget and the same frontier LLM backbone, open-source state-of-the-art harnesses provide no advantages over a single session of a minimal-harness coding agent baseline, pointing to the backbone as the primary driver for performance. Via a series of large-scale systematic ablation studies, we argue that the machinery layers become redundant in the coding agent setting. We conclude that the effort spent elaborating hand-crafted harnesses around strong models yields poor returns for current MLE benchmarks.

signals.brief_en:
Title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?

Recent autonomous machine‑learning‑engineering (MLE) agents have closed gaps on public leaderboards, often driven by stagnation in long‑horizon cycles and limited LLM primitives. Consequently, many systems now sit atop complex harnesses—multi‑agent orchestrators, dedicated retrieval sub‑agents, etc. However, the alternative of a minimal‑harness coding agent—where a frontier LLM directly reads, writes, and executes code—has been under‑explored. Our systematic, large‑scale ablations show that, given equal compute time and the same state‑of‑the‑art LLM backbone, open‑source elaborate harnesses do not outperform a single‑session minimal coding agent. The backbone model, not the surrounding machinery, appears to be the primary performance driver. Additional layers become redundant in this setting, suggesting that further hand‑crafted harness development yields diminishing returns on current MLE benchmarks.

signals.title: Skill-Based AI Agents for Power-System Studies
signals.content: This paper describes a skill-based agentic framework for power-system studies using Model Context Protocol (MCP)-connected engineering tools. A custom MCP server was developed to expose Siemens PTI PSSE functions for power-flow analysis, dynamic simulation, result extraction, and model-validation workflows. Two implementation pathways built on a programmable OpenAI Agents software development kit (SDK) and a Claude Code command-line interface (CLI) were evaluated, both using reusable skills, subagents, MCP tools, data-repository connections, and local shell/Python execution. Both frontier-model-based implementations successfully executed representative study tasks. Success was evaluated based on task completion, output accuracy, and the need for human expert interventions. Results based on public datasets show that agentic systems can greatly accelerate power system dynamic simulation process for transmission planning studies leveraging industry-grade simulation platforms. This points toward a shift in transmission planning practice, where agentic systems could handle routine simulation setup and result extraction, allowing engineers to focus expert judgment on scenario design and interpretation rather than tool operation.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Skill-Based AI Agents for Power-System Studies

This paper presents a skill‑based agentic framework that links engineering tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for power‑system studies. A custom MCP server exposes Siemens PTI PSSE functions for power‑flow analysis, dynamic simulation, result extraction, and model‑validation workflows. Two implementation paths were tested: one using the OpenAI Agents SDK and another using the Claude Code CLI. Both rely on reusable skills, sub‑agents, MCP‑connected tools, data‑repository links, and local shell/Python execution. The frontier‑model implementations successfully completed representative study tasks, with performance measured by task completion, output accuracy, and the extent of required human expert intervention. Public‑dataset results indicate that agentic systems can markedly accelerate dynamic simulation for transmission planning, suggesting a future where routine simulation setup and result extraction are automated, allowing engineers to concentrate on scenario design and interpretation rather than tool operation.

signals.title: EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery
signals.content: Evolutionary search with large language models (LLMs) can stall when progress requires external knowledge the model lacks. Supplying relevant documents helps, but simply adding web search tool can keep returning the same pages as solutions change. We introduce EvoDuet, a bi-level optimization method that co-evolves solutions and search queries with fixed model parameters. At each iteration, a retrieval gate lets the LLM assess its knowledge gap and choose to retrieve new documents, reuse stored ones, or proceed without them. An inner loop refines queries and ranks documents by the solution scores they are predicted to yield; an outer loop generates candidates in parallel from these documents and records the evaluated outcomes for later searches. Across 21 optimization tasks with one candidate per iteration, EvoDuet raises OpenEvolve's normalized discovery gain from 74.1% to 78.0% with GPT-5.6-Luna and from 61.3% to 82.3% with Gemini-3.8-Flash, whereas Qwen3.5-9B does not benefit. Our best runs surpass the previously reported best scores on eight tasks, including Swap Reduction on Q20 and Rosetta, and match them on three more. EvoDuet also improves with other scaffolds (e.g., Top-K, EvoX) on Sums/Diffs and Denoising, demonstrating its applicability across evolutionary search scaffolds.

signals.brief_en: EvoDuet is a bi‑level optimization framework that jointly evolves task solutions and web‑search queries while keeping the LLM parameters fixed. A retrieval gate lets the model decide whether to fetch new documents, reuse stored ones, or continue without external data, based on its assessed knowledge gap. The inner loop refines queries and ranks documents by the expected improvement they can bring to the solution; the outer loop generates candidate solutions in parallel using those documents and records their outcomes for future searches. In tests on 21 scientific‑discovery tasks, EvoDuet raised OpenEvolve’s normalized discovery gain from 74.1% to 78.0% with GPT‑5.6‑Luna and from 61.3% to 82.3% with Gemini‑3.8‑Flash, while Qwen3.5‑9B showed no benefit. The method set new best scores on eight tasks and matched the best on three, and it also improved performance when combined with other evolutionary scaffolds such as Top‑K and EvoX.
signals.brief_ar: EvoDuet هو إطار تحسين ثنائي المستوى يطوّر حلول المهام واستعلامات البحث على الويب بشكل متزامن مع إبقاء معلمات نموذج اللغة الكبيرة ثابتة. يتيح بوّابة الاسترجاع للنموذج اتخاذ قرار بجلب مستندات جديدة، أو إعادة استخدام المستندات المخزنة، أو المتابعة دون بيانات خارجية بناءً على الفجوة المعرفية التي يحددها. الحلقة الداخلية تُحسّن الاستعلامات وتُصنّف المستندات وفقًا للتحسين المتوقع الذي قد تقدّمه للحلول؛ الحلقة الخارجية تُولّد حلولًا مرشّحة بالتوازي باستخدام تلك المستندات وتُسجّل نتائجها لاستخدامها في عمليات البحث المستقبلية. في تجارب على 21 مهمة اكتشاف علمي، رفع EvoDuet معدل الاكتشاف المُعَدل من 74.1٪ إلى 78.0٪ مع GPT‑5.6‑Luna ومن 61.3٪ إلى 82.3٪ مع Gemini‑3.8‑Flash، بينما لم يُظهر Qwen3.5‑9B فائدة. حقق الأسلوب أفضل النتائج على ثمانية مهام وتساوى مع الأفضل في ثلاثة أخرى، كما حسّن الأداء عند دمجه مع هياكل تطورية أخرى مثل Top‑K وEvoX.

signals.content: 『PROJECT MAVEN』輪講 今日の範囲で示されたのは、Project Mavenが単なる「AIによるドローン映像解析」ではないということ。 背景にあるのは、米軍が長年抱えてきた「情報は大量にあるのに、戦場で使える形にできない」という課題。 湾岸戦争、アフガニスタン、イラクと、兵器は精密化していく一方、情報処理はWord、Excel、PowerPoint、Google Earthに依存。 Palantirは、ばらばらの情報をつなぎ、人・場所・出来事の関係を可視化した。 しかし、それでも大量の映像や情報を人間だけで処理するには限界がある。 そこでProject Maven。 本質は、 センサー → 情報統合 → AI分析 → 標的識別 → 意思決定 → 攻撃 という一連のターゲティング・プロセスを、AI前提で組み直すこと。 さらに重要なのは、AIモデルだけでなく、軍人・情報分析官・技術者を混成した小規模チームをつくり、調達や組織運営そのものまで変えようとした点。 つまりProject Mavenは、AI兵器の話であると同時に、「情報をどう意思決定と行動に変えるか」という組織変革の話でもある。 そして、これは軍事に限らない。 本邦でもバズったDXも結局、 既存業務にAIや新しいソフトウェアを足す話ではなく、 「データ、意思決定、業務プロセス、組織そのものを再設計できるか」 という話なのだと思う。
